expectations.text: States the problem is structural rather than a matter of awareness, and rejects promoting the existing dashboard as the fix
expectations.evidence: "Promoting the dashboard harder won't fix this. The dashboard is good. It's pointed at the wrong audience."

expectations.text: Explains that a per-account dashboard cannot serve an ISV whose app is installed across thousands of accounts, because nobody watches thousands of dashboards
expectations.evidence: Quotes the skill: "a per-account dashboard is structurally useless to them: nobody watches a thousand dashboards."

expectations.text: Requires cross-install aggregation keyed on the app or client ID, spanning every install of one ISV's app, as the missing surface
expectations.evidence: "No per-app view. Nothing aggregates by app across installs"; "a partner-scoped cross-install view".

expectations.text: Requires push notification to the ISV rather than relying on them to come and look
expectations.evidence: "No push... it can only be pulled, never pushed"; per-app digest and state-change alerts.

expectations.text: Identifies the access model as a distinct gap: the ISV engineer who maintains the integration is typically not a user of the customer's account and therefore cannot open the per-account dashboard at all
expectations.evidence: "The ISV's engineers usually aren't admins of those accounts... an access-model gap, not a logging gap."

expectations.text: Distinguishes the single-account integrator segment from the ISV-fleet segment, and states that a surface designed for the first does not finish the job for the second
expectations.evidence: Three-segment table; "Your dashboard serves the first segment well. Your 22 ISVs are the second."

expectations.text: Recommends an installs-affected against installs-total measure per ISV app, and reads that ratio as the diagnosis
expectations.evidence: Used for ranking and alert content ("blast radius"), but the ratio is never read as a diagnosis of the failure cause.

expectations.text: Interprets a high installs-affected ratio as a partner-side release and a low one as configuration trouble at a few customers
expectations.evidence: No such interpretation. Only "app X is failing on 200 of 240 installs" appears as an example.

expectations.text: Does not conclude that Tuliphase's existing per-account request log was the wrong thing to have built
expectations.evidence: "The dashboard is good."

expectations.text: Recommends deciding explicitly who can read each surface: the account owner, any user of the account, and the partner engineer outside the account
expectations.evidence: Names ISV engineers outside customer accounts, customer admins for the per-customer dashboard, and a separate cross-tenant data-classification decision for the ISV view.

expectations.text: Scopes the notification audience to the 22 ISVs rather than to the individual customer accounts
expectations.evidence: "Send a per-app digest to a named partner contact"; "Collect a named technical alert contact per ISV."
